```{r}
#| include: FALSE

library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(httr)
library(tidycensus)
```


```{r}
#creating tibble that includes the variables of interest
wow <- tibble(
  movie = character(), 
  year = integer(), 
  release_date = character(),
  director = character(), 
  movie_duration = character(), 
  timestamp = character(),
  full_line = character(),
  current_wow_in_movie = double(),
  total_wows_in_movie = double(),
  video = list()
)

#create a for loop to get each distinct "wow" moment from the randomly generated moments given by the url
#loop 100 times to find each distinict moment - there are 91 "wow" moments

for(i in 1:100) {
  url <- str_c("https://owen-wilson-wow-api.onrender.com/wows/random?results=100")
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  onemovie <- GET(url)
  details <- content(onemovie, "parsed")
 
#for every wow moment found, takes the variables of interest and puts them into the tibble 
  for(j in 1:length(details)) {
    wow <- bind_rows(wow, tibble(
      movie = details[[j]]$movie,
      year = details[[j]]$year,
      release_date = details[[j]]$release_date,
      director = details[[j]]$director,
      movie_duration = details[[j]]$movie_duration,
      timestamp = details[[j]]$timestamp,
      full_line = details[[j]]$full_line,
      current_wow_in_movie = as.numeric(details[[j]]$current_wow_in_movie),
      total_wows_in_movie = as.numeric(details[[j]]$total_wows_in_movie),
      video = list(details[[j]]$video)
    ))
  }
}

#final "wow" tibble
wow <- wow |>
  distinct(full_line, timestamp, movie, .keep_all = TRUE)

wow

```

## Variables in the CSV: 

- Year
- Release Date
- Director
- Character
- Movie Duration
- Timestamp
- Full Line
- Current Wow in Movie
- Total Wows in Movie
- Video

## Reflection

To make this final csv, we used GitHub branches and pull requests to edit on our own time. There were a lot of technical difficulties with Git, where we would do all the correct steps and Git wouldn't recognize that any changes were made and/or pull requests active. Working in the branches worked well for when we were on our own, but when we were working in person together, using GitHub added some unnecessary complications. In the future, we may use branches to edit on our own time, but make changes directly on the main project when we are together and can talk about changes we are making.
